resources.string: Shows the shift you are on today and when you are next in.
Notifies you the evening before a working day.
Pick the rotation you work, and Shiftly fills in your calendar for every month ahead.
Choose one below, or build your own if it isn\'t listed. You can change it later.
Right shifts, wrong days? Move the whole rotation without rebuilding it. Days you changed by hand stay where they are.
Pick the first day of your next \"%1$s\" cycle — the first day back on after a block off.
Tap a shift for each day of your cycle, in order. Add days until the pattern repeats.
Tap a day to remove it
Pick the date you\'ll be on day 1 of this cycle.
Only this day changes — your rotation stays as it is.
Tell Shiftly your rotation once. It fills in every month, forwards and back, for as long as you work it.
Your rotation repeats — that\'s the whole idea
Most shift work runs on a cycle: four on and four off, two-two-three, a week of days then a week of nights. Whatever yours is, it repeats.

So Shiftly only needs two things from you: what one full cycle looks like, and which real date you are on day 1 of it. From those it works out every other day by itself. There is nothing to fill in each week.
Every day is a coloured square. The colour and the letter tell you which shift it is.
Filled in the colour of that shift, with its letter underneath.
Pale and unlettered, so a run of days off is obvious at a glance.
Ringed, with the date in bold. The Today button in the top bar brings you back to it from any month.
The red dot means this day no longer follows the rotation because you set it by hand.
The three numbers at the top
Shifts is how many working days fall in the month you are looking at. Days off is the rest of the month. Hours adds up the length of every shift in it — useful for checking a payslip.
They follow whichever month is on screen, so scroll forward to see what next month holds.
Tap any day and pick a different shift. Swapped a shift with someone, took a day\'s leave, got called in — this is for that.

Only that one day changes. Your rotation is left alone, so the rest of the year does not move. The day gets a red dot to show it was you, not the rotation. Tap it again and press Reset to put it back.
The bar at the bottom of the calendar shows the rotation you are on. Tap it, or the pencil in the top bar, to pick a different one or build your own.
Changing your rotation clears the single days you had changed by hand. Those were corrections to the old rotation and would be wrong against the new one.
Everything is off by a day or two

This is the usual thing to go wrong, and it is not worth rebuilding your rotation over. It means the start date you gave is out — the shape of your cycle is right, it is just sitting on the wrong dates.

Open your rotation from the bar at the bottom of the calendar. At the top you will find buttons to move the whole rotation a day earlier or a day later. Nudge it until the calendar matches the shifts you actually worked this week. Days you changed by hand stay put.
Shiftly comes with a widget showing the shift you are on today and when you are next in. Long-press an empty part of your homescreen, choose Widgets, and find Shiftly in the list.
If you allow notifications, Shiftly reminds you the evening before any working day. Nothing on days off.
Your schedule stays on your phone
There is no account and no sign-in, and your rotation is not sent anywhere. It is stored on this phone only, which also means uninstalling the app deletes it.
Four 12-hour days, then four days off. 8-day cycle.
Four days on, four off, four nights on, four off. 16-day cycle.
2 on, 2 off, 3 on, 2 off, 2 on, 3 off. 14-day cycle.
A full 2-2-3 rotation on days, then the same on nights. 28-day cycle.
The classic 28-day 12-hour rotation, ending in a full week off.
Three 12-hour days on, three off. 6-day cycle.
A full week on, a full week off. 14-day cycle.
A standard working week. Anchor it to a Monday. 7-day cycle.
Six on, two off — drifts through the week. 8-day cycle.
Week of days, week of nights
Five days on, two off, five nights on, two off. 14-day cycle.
A 24-hour tour, then two days off. 3-day cycle.
Two 24-hour tours back to back, then four days off. 6-day cycle.
Three 24-hour tours on alternate days, then four days off. 9-day cycle.
